items.author: Simon Goodley
items.summary: Analysts predict that President Trump's deal to import Russian diesel will have minimal impact on US fuel prices due to insufficient quantities and logistical delays. Experts also note that damage to Russian refineries makes the full delivery of the promised fuel unlikely.

items.title: Nobel Prize for economics awarded to Hall and Woodford for work on ‘smoothing’ crises
items.author: Graeme Wearden
items.summary: US economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford have been awarded the 2026 Nobel economics prize for developing models that help central bankers stabilize economies. Their research provides a theoretical framework for managing business cycles and inflation through tools like forward guidance.

also.title: Congratulations to the Hoover Institution's Robert E. Hall, on His Economics Nobel Prize

brief.what: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford were awarded the 2026 Nobel economics prize for creating the 'microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation.' Their work, which includes the New Keynesian model, provides policymakers with tools to manage economic peaks and troughs, helping to avoid runaway inflation and deep recessions.
brief.who: Robert E. Hall of Stanford University and Michael Woodford of Columbia University are the laureates, recognized by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences for their contributions to economic policy.
brief.context: The laureates' models improved upon traditional Keynesian theories that struggled during the 1970s oil shocks. Their framework has been widely adopted by central banks and finance ministries to navigate crises, including the 2008 financial crisis and the Covid pandemic.
brief.why: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences stated the pair generated a 'paradigm shift in stabilisation policy' by explaining how individual household and business behaviors collectively influence the broader economy. John Hassler, chair of the economics prize committee, noted their work provides a stable theoretical foundation for modern economic management.

items.title: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
items.summary: A Ukrainian national is on trial in Hamburg, Germany, accused of orchestrating the 2022 sabotage of the Nord Stream gas pipelines. Prosecutors allege the operation was carried out by military personnel to disrupt Russian energy revenue.

also.note: The Financial Times headline specifically identifies the defendant as an 'ex-officer,' emphasizing his military background more directly than the BBC.

brief.what: The trial of Serhii K, a Ukrainian national, has commenced in Hamburg regarding the 2022 destruction of three of the four Nord Stream gas pipelines. German prosecutors allege the suspect led a team of divers and explosives experts to sabotage the infrastructure, which they classify as a war crime.
brief.who: The primary defendant is Serhii K, a former Ukrainian military officer. German federal prosecutors are leading the case, while Ukrainian officials, including President Volodymyr Zelensky, have denied state involvement in the blasts.
brief.context: The Nord Stream pipelines were critical energy infrastructure connecting Russia to Germany. The sabotage occurred seven months after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, during a period of heightened geopolitical tension and shifting European energy policies.
brief.why: German prosecutors state the trial is necessary because the attack undermined Germany's internal security and violated international law. Conversely, some Ukrainian officials argue the pipelines were tools of Russian war preparation, while others maintain the investigation is merely one version of events.
brief.next: The trial is ongoing in Hamburg, while a second suspect, Volodymyr Zhuravlov, awaits potential extradition from Croatia to face related charges.

items.title: NFL tickets discounted to fill Wembley Stadium
items.author: Matt Hardy
items.summary: The NFL is offering ticket discounts at Wembley Stadium to ensure a full crowd for this weekend's game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Houston Texans. This follows recent struggles to sell out international fixtures in London.

brief.what: The NFL is discounting tickets for the upcoming Jacksonville Jaguars and Houston Texans game at Wembley Stadium to avoid failing to reach a 90,000-person capacity. Discounts of 25 per cent are being applied to specific lower-tier blocks, with prices starting at £99 for standard seats.
